newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Caymans sets bill on freezing assets of criminals.
newsitem.headline: Caymans sets bill on freezing assets of criminals.

text.p: The Cayman Islands parliament Wednesday passed a bill to make it easier to investigate and freeze assets of foreign criminals.
But the Proceeds of Criminal Conduct Bill, which was passed on Tuesday, was amended to insure that tax cases from other jurisdictions were not considered.
There are no direct taxes in the Caymans and the territory does not recognize tax convictions or problems from other jurisdictions, said Attorney General Richard Coles.
All British dependent territories were scheduled to enact similar legislation, but the Caymans became the first of the territories to actually pass the law, Coles said.
The measure's intention is to "hit the criminal masterminds who invariably do not get caught," he said.
The law is similar to the islands' Misuse of Drugs Law, which allows its government to investigate and seize assets of people convicted of drug crimes elsewhere.

One provision of the new legislation that was bitterly opposed by the real estate and legal professions in the Caymans requires "service providers" to report to the authorities anyone they suspect of being "unscrupulous investors" engaging in or benefitting from crime.
The provision will require that real estate agents, bankers, lawyers and other "service providers" in ther islands will require banking, police and legal references from foreign investors.
